lessons.title: Document Processing and Analysis
lessons.description:
Solution Breakdown:
Automation Summary
Trigger & Ingestion
Monitors a specific Google Drive folder for newly added files (every minute).
Automatically downloads each new file, converting Google Docs/Sheets/Slides to PDF if needed.
Format Routing
Detects MIME type and splits processing:
PDFs → text extraction
Spreadsheets (XLSX) → table data extraction and aggregation
Data Preparation
Normalizes outputs into two core fields:
text: the extracted content
document link: a shareable Drive URL
AI-Powered Classification & Extraction
Uses a GPT-4–based agent to:
Classify the document as Invoice, Resume, Contract, or Report
Extract key entities (e.g., Name, Date, Company, Amount, Purpose)
Summarize in 2–3 sentences
Decides which Slack channel to notify based on classification:
#finance for invoices/expenses
#hr for resumes/talent files
#legal for contracts and legal docs
Automated Notification
Posts the extracted details, summary, and link into the appropriate Slack channel
---
Business Case / Use Case
A “Smart Document Router” that eliminates manual triage of incoming files and instantly delivers key information to the right team via Slack.
Value Proposition
Speed & Efficiency: Cuts human routing time from minutes/hours to seconds.
Accuracy & Consistency: Reduces misclassification and ensures no file gets overlooked.
Centralized Oversight: Keeps a searchable archive of processed documents with metadata.
Ideal Scenarios
High-Volume Invoicing: Agencies or consultancies receiving dozens of client invoices daily.
Recruitment Pipelines: HR teams processing hundreds of resumes from a shared drive.
Contract Management: Legal departments needing instant alerts on new agreements.
Reporting Workflows: Operations teams that drop regular status or compliance reports into Drive.
Target Industries
Professional Services (Accounting, Legal, Consulting)
Staffing & Recruitment Firms
Logistics & Manufacturing (invoice and compliance report handling)
Real Estate & Property Management (leases/contracts)
Healthcare Administration (patient forms, insurance claims)By packaging this as a managed service or low-code integration, you can offer clients a plug-and-play solution to streamline their document workflows, reduce overhead, and improve SLA compliance.

lessons.title: Content Personalization Engine
lessons.description:
Solution Breakdown:
Automation Summary
RSS Feed Polling (every minute): Watches a specified RSS feed URL for newly published articles.
Relevancy Classification: Sends each item’s title, description, and link to a GPT-4O–based “Check Relevancy” node, which outputs {"relevant":"Yes/No","reasoning":…}.
Content Filtering: Only passes through articles tagged "relevant":"Yes" via an n8n Filter node.
Article Retrieval & Cleaning:
Fetches the full article HTML from its URL.
Strips HTML noise and formats the core text via Markdown and a “Clean the Article” GPT-4O node.
AI-Driven Content Generation: Uses a LangChain “agent” with GPT-4O to:
Research the topic via an external “Research Assistant” HTTP call.
Produce a finalized Instagram-style post: Title, Caption, Hashtags, and a 120–130-word script in the brand’s voice.
Content Persistence: Inserts the generated fields (Title, Script, Hashtags, Caption, Source info) into an Airtable “Content” table for review or publishing.
---
Business Case / Use Case
A “Content Personalization Engine” that continually scans industry news, filters for brand-relevant articles, enriches them with AI research, and auto-generates on-brand social media posts—ready to publish or schedule.
Value Proposition
Scale & Speed: Produces polished, platform-optimized content—in under minutes—for daily or multiple-times-daily posting.
Brand Consistency: Enforces a unified voice, format, and compliance with content guidelines across all output.
Resource Efficiency: Reduces reliance on manual curation, copywriting, and research, freeing marketing teams for strategy and high-level tasks.
Data-Driven Optimization: Captures performance data in Airtable for A/B testing of hooks, formats, and hashtags.
---
Ideal Industries & Buyers
Digital Media & Publishing: Tech blogs, news sites, and vertical-specific magazines needing constant social feed curation.
Marketing & Creative Agencies: Managing social platforms for multiple clients with distinct brand voices.
SaaS & Technology Firms: Educating users on product updates, industry trends, and best practices via social channels.
E-Commerce & Retail Brands: Amplifying product launches, sales events, and lifestyle content at scale.
Professional Services: Consultants and thought-leadership firms aiming to maintain a steady stream of value-add posts.
Influencer & Community Managers: Automated, personalized content pipelines to engage followers without manual drafting.

lessons.title: Data Integration and Transformation Hub
lessons.description:
Solution Breakdown:
Automation Summary
Monthly Schedule Trigger: Automatically kicks off the workflow on a monthly interval.
Fetch Facebook Ad Data: Calls the Facebook Graph API to pull daily campaign insights (spend, impressions, clicks, leads, purchases).
Fetch Lead Pipeline Data: Reads a Google Sheets “Lead Campaign Pipeline” sheet for budget allocations, funnel-stage metrics, and manual notes.
Data Aggregation & Merge: Aggregates spreadsheet rows into a single JSON array under lead and merges with the Facebook data stream, producing a unified dataset.
AI-Driven Analysis & Report Generation: Feeds the combined data into a LangChain “AI Agent” (using model o3) with a tailored system prompt to compute KPIs (CPC, CPL, CPR), CTR, funnel conversion rates, anomaly detection, and optimization recommendations—then formats a clear, structured weekly summary.
Automated Google Doc Creation & Population: Creates a Google Doc titled “Campaign Report for {Month}” and inserts the AI-generated report content into it, ready for stakeholder review.
---
Business Case / Use Case
Modern marketing teams spend hours each week manually collecting ad metrics, reconciling them with internal lead-tracking spreadsheets, and crafting performance summaries. This “Data Integration & Transformation Hub” streamlines the entire process:
Hands-Off Reporting
Eliminates manual data exports from Facebook Ads and internal sheets.
Ensures consistency and removes human error in KPI calculations.
Actionable Insights Delivered Fast
AI-powered analysis highlights over- and under-performing campaigns, spots anomalies, and recommends budget shifts in seconds.
Instant Google Doc generation accelerates stakeholder reviews and approvals.
Scalable & Repeatable
Once configured, the workflow scales across multiple clients or business units with minimal setup.
Frees analysts to focus on strategy rather than data wrangling.Ideal Pitch: Sell this managed integration to digital marketing agencies or in-house marketing teams as a “Performance Reporting as a Service” module—complete with setup, template prompts, and monitoring—so they can onboard new clients or campaigns in days instead of weeks, while guaranteeing weekly insights without lifting a finger.

---
Industries That Benefit Most
Digital Marketing & Ad Agencies: Automate client-report deliverables and KPI dashboards.
E-Commerce & Retail Brands: Align ad spend with lead and sales funnels across platforms.
SaaS & Technology Companies: Regularly report on trial sign-ups, demos, and paid conversions.
Professional Services Firms (Consulting, Finance): Combine marketing outreach with lead pipeline data for executive reporting.
Media & Publishing: Correlate ad buys with subscription or content-driven lead metrics.Each of these sectors relies on timely, accurate performance reports—making this turnkey solution a compelling upsell for any organization looking to scale its marketing analytics without adding headcount.

lessons.title: Smart Action Agent
lessons.description:
Solution Breakdown:
Automation Summary
Slack-triggered workflow: Listens for any new message (including audio files) in a designated Slack channel.
Audio handling: Downloads the attached audio file via Slack’s API.
Transcription: Sends the audio to OpenAI’s speech‐to‐text endpoint to produce a text transcript.
Intelligent action parsing: Feeds the transcript into a GPT-powered “Smart Action Agent” that interprets user intent and maps it to available tools — without follow-up questions.
Calendar automation: If the user requests a meeting or event, the agent extracts date, time, summary, and description (defaulting missing parameters) and calls the Google Calendar tool to create the event.
Lead management in Trello:
Add new leads: Retrieves Trello list IDs for the lead pipeline, then creates a new card in “New Lead” (or specified) stage with extracted name and details.
Update existing leads: Fetches all pipeline lists and cards, locates the specified lead card, and updates its description or moves it to a new stage as instructed.
---
Business Case / Use Case
Solution Name: Smart Action Agent
Core Offering: A conversational AI assistant embedded in Slack that executes scheduling and CRM updates on behalf of users, turning natural-language or voice notes directly into calendar events or Trello pipeline actions.
Key Benefits
Seamless Workflow: Users never leave Slack to schedule meetings or update leads, reducing context switching.
Hands-Free Productivity: Audio commands allow busy professionals to multitask—e.g., schedule a follow-up while driving or update prospect status on the go.
Consistency & Compliance: Default parameters and structured prompts ensure every event and lead card adheres to organizational standards.Ideal Industries & Buyers
Sales & Business Development (B2B SaaS, Professional Services): Rapidly capture and qualify leads during calls or meetings, then automatically schedule demos or follow-ups.
Recruitment & Staffing: Recruiters can transcribe candidate screening calls and instantly update applicant pipelines without manual data entry.
Consulting & Agencies: Consultants can log project kickoff meetings and onboard new client leads via simple voice notes in Slack.
Real Estate: Agents can record property visit notes in Slack and have the system update their CRM board or schedule client calls.
Executive Assistants / Admin Teams: Assistants can use brief audio messages to build executive calendars and maintain contact pipelines with minimal effort.By packaging this as a low-code n8n integration or managed Slack app, you can offer clients a plug-and-play “voice-to-action” assistant that drives productivity, accelerates response times, and enforces process consistency across any team that relies on Slack, Google Calendar, and Trello.

lessons.title: Customer Inquiry Router
lessons.description:
Solution Breakdown:
Summary of the Automation Workflow
Trigger: Listens for incoming customer chat messages via an n8n LangChain chatTrigger node.
Classification & Extraction: Uses a custom AI Agent to
Classify the inquiry as Sales, Technical Support, or General
Pull out key entities (e.g. Name, Email, Date, Urgency, Query)
Generate a 2–3 sentence summary of the request
Notification: Posts a formatted message into the appropriate Slack channel (#tech-support, #sales, or #general) with all extracted details and the summary
Ticket Creation: Automatically creates a Trello card in the support board, setting the title, description, and priority label (High/Medium/Low) based on the extracted urgency
Orchestration: Coordinates calls between the OpenAI Chat model (gpt-4o) and the Slack/Trello nodes to keep the entire flow seamless and hands-off
---
Business Case / Use Case
A mid-sized B2B software company typically fields hundreds of inbound inquiries daily—from demo requests and billing questions to troubleshooting and feature asks. Manually triaging and routing these messages not only delays customer response times but also forces highly paid engineers to handle routine classification tasks. By deploying this n8n-based “Customer Inquiry Router,” the company can:
Reduce Response Times: Customers get an immediate acknowledgement via the correct support channel, cutting average wait times by up to 50%.
Optimize Human Effort: Sales and support teams focus on high-value interactions instead of sorting and copying/pasting details.
Maintain SLAs Automatically: Priority labels in Trello enforce escalation workflows for high-urgency issues, ensuring nothing slips through the cracks.
Scale Without Headcount: As inquiry volume grows, the same automation handles surges without needing to hire more triage staff.This solution can be packaged as a “plug-and-play” support-ops module, with training and customization offered as professional services.

---
Industries That Would Benefit
SaaS & Cloud Services: Large volumes of demo requests, technical queries, and billing questions
E-commerce & Retail: Order issues, returns, product questions, and payment support
Telecommunications: Service outages, device troubleshooting, plan changes
Financial Services: Account inquiries, transaction disputes, loan application status
Healthcare Providers: Appointment scheduling, billing inquiries, general patient questionsEach of these sectors relies on rapid, accurate customer support routing—and can unlock both cost savings and improved satisfaction by automating the classification and ticket-creation steps.

lessons.title: Lead Qualification and Routing
lessons.description:
Solution Breakdown:
Automation Summary
Webhook Trigger: Listens for incoming lead data (name, contact info, company details, message, tech stack, budget, etc.) via a webhook endpoint.
AI-Powered Lead Scoring: Feeds the raw lead JSON into a GPT-4 agent that:
Evaluates “Fit” (company size, industry, location)
Assesses “Role” (decision-making authority)
Gauges “Intent” (message content, CTA clicked, UTM source)
Rates “Urgency” (timeline mentioned) and “Engagement” (tech stack, source behavior)
Outputs a numeric score (0–100), a tier (Hot/Warm/Cold), recommended routing, and reasoning.
Sales Rep Assignment: Searches an Airtable “Sales Rep” table to pick the appropriate rep based on tier (e.g. Hot → Senior, Warm → Junior) and current workload.
Lead Record Creation: Creates a new record in the Airtable “Leads” table, populating fields like Name, Email, Tier, Score, Assigned Rep, and original lead details.
Slack Notification: Posts a formatted summary of the lead analysis and assignment into the #sales Slack channel for immediate visibility.
---
Business Case / Use Case
Solution: A fully automated “Lead Qualification & Routing” workflow that turns raw inbound inquiries into scored, tiered leads, assigns them to the right sales rep, and alerts your team — all within seconds.
Value Proposition
Faster Response Times: High-value (“Hot”) leads get flagged and routed to senior reps instantly, reducing your time-to-contact from hours to minutes.
Consistent Qualification: AI applies uniform criteria across every lead, ensuring no opportunity is overlooked or misrouted.
Sales Efficiency: Reduces manual triage work for SDR teams by up to 70%, letting them focus on engagement rather than data entry.
Scalable Operations: Handles spikes in lead volume (e.g., after a marketing campaign) without adding headcount.Ideal Industries
B2B SaaS & Tech: High incoming demo requests and feature inquiries that must be prioritized.
Professional Services & Consultancy: Inbound RFIs (requests for information) that require fast, consistent follow-up.
Financial Services & Insurance: Web-form leads needing quick qualification for credit or policy sales.
Recruitment & Staffing Agencies: Candidate vs. client lead sorting and routing to specialized consultants.
Real Estate & Property Management: Buyer/seller inquiries triaged to agents based on priority and location.By packaging this as a turnkey integration—complete with setup, templates, and ongoing tuning—you can offer clients a plug-and-play sales-ops enhancement that delivers rapid ROI and scales with their growth.

Evaluates “Fit” (company size, industry, location)
Assesses “Role” (decision-making authority)
Gauges “Intent” (message content, CTA clicked, UTM source)
Rates “Urgency” (timeline mentioned) and “Engagement” (tech stack, source behavior)
Outputs a numeric score (0–100), a tier (Hot/Warm/Cold), recommended routing, and reasoning.
Sales Rep Assignment
: Searches an Airtable “Sales Rep” table to pick the appropriate rep based on tier (e.g. Hot → Senior, Warm → Junior) and current workload.
Lead Record Creation
: Creates a new record in the Airtable “Leads” table, populating fields like Name, Email, Tier, Score, Assigned Rep, and original lead details.
Slack Notification
: Posts a formatted summary of the lead analysis and assignment into the #sales Slack channel for immediate visibility.
Business Case / Use Case
Solution
: A fully automated “Lead Qualification & Routing” workflow that turns raw inbound inquiries into scored, tiered leads, assigns them to the right sales rep, and alerts your team — all within seconds.
Value Proposition
Faster Response Times
: High-value (“Hot”) leads get flagged and routed to senior reps instantly, reducing your time-to-contact from hours to minutes.
Consistent Qualification
: AI applies uniform criteria across every lead, ensuring no opportunity is overlooked or misrouted.
Sales Efficiency
: Reduces manual triage work for SDR teams by up to 70%, letting them focus on engagement rather than data entry.
Scalable Operations
: Handles spikes in lead volume (e.g., after a marketing campaign) without adding headcount.
Ideal Industries
B2B SaaS & Tech
: High incoming demo requests and feature inquiries that must be prioritized.
Professional Services & Consultancy
: Inbound RFIs (requests for information) that require fast, consistent follow-up.
Financial Services & Insurance
: Web-form leads needing quick qualification for credit or policy sales.
Recruitment & Staffing Agencies
: Candidate vs. client lead sorting and routing to specialized consultants.
Real Estate & Property Management
: Buyer/seller inquiries triaged to agents based on priority and location.

By packaging this as a turnkey integration—complete with setup, templates, and ongoing tuning—you can offer clients a plug-and-play sales-ops enhancement that delivers rapid ROI and scales with their growth.

lessons.title: Meeting Summarizer and Action Item Tracker
lessons.description:
Solution Breakdown:
Automation Summary
Webhook Trigger
Listens for “Transcription Completed” events (e.g. from Fireflies.ai) carrying a meetingId.
Transcript Retrieval
Calls Fireflies.ai’s GraphQL API to fetch the full meeting transcript, metadata (date, speakers), and any built-in summary.
AI-Driven Extraction
Feeds the transcript JSON into a GPT-powered “AI Agent” with a system prompt to extract, in structured JSON:
Next Steps (shorthand directives on what to do next)
Action Items (bullet-list of tasks, assignees if possible)
Key Topics discussed
Proposal Required? (Yes/No based on client intent)
Client Follow-Up details (draft copy for follow-up emails or tasks)
Automated Notifications & Deliverables
Slack Posting
Posts the extracted summary & action items into a designated Slack channel for the team to review.
Proposal Drafting (conditional)
If a proposal is deemed necessary, the agent:
Estimates hours & cost (e.g. $150/hr)
Generates a basic draft proposal (plain formatting)
Email Delivery
Sends the draft proposal via SMTP to an internal reviewer (e.g., the project admin) for final edits/approval.
---
Business Case / Use Case
Solution: A “Meeting Summaries & Action-Item Generator” that transforms raw recorded meetings into clear next steps, assigned tasks, and even preliminary proposals—delivered automatically to team channels and inboxes.
Key Benefits
Eliminate Manual Note-Taking: Frees meeting participants from having to jot down action items, letting them focus on discussion.
Faster Follow-Up: Teams see next steps and draft follow-up communication immediately after call completion.
Consistency & Accountability: Every meeting yields a standardized summary, reducing miscommunication and missed tasks.
Integrated Proposal Workflow: Automatically identifies when a formal proposal is needed and produces a first draft—accelerating sales or project kick-off.
---

Consulting & Professional Services
– High-value client calls where rapid, accurate follow-up and proposals drive revenue.
Sales & Business Development
– Discovery calls that need instant summaries, follow-up emails, and quote proposals.
Agencies (Marketing, Design, Development)
– Kick-off and status meetings feeding directly into project management and estimates.
Recruitment & Staffing
– Candidate screening calls summarized for hiring managers, with action items for next steps.
Remote-First Tech Teams
– Distributed teams relying on recorded stand-ups or planning sessions for clear task handoffs.
Legal & Finance
– Client consultations requiring precise record-keeping, task assignment, and engagement proposals.By packaging this as a managed Slack/Fireflies integration or an “add-on” for any transcript service, you can offer organizations a plug-and-play way to capture meeting intelligence, drive accountability, and shorten the sales-to-proposal cycle.

lessons.title: ASMR Video Pipeline
lessons.description: This workflow automates the creation and distribution of ASMR-style cutting videos using AI. It generates creative concepts for videos showing materials being sliced (like "obsidian shaped like a chess piece"), creates multiple video clips and matching sounds using AI services (Wavespeed and Fal AI), stitches them together into a final video, and then automatically publishes the content across nine social media platforms (Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Threads, Twitter, LinkedIn, Bluesky, and Pinterest) via the Blotato API, while tracking everything in Google Sheets.

lessons.title: Prompt-to-HTML Tailwind Renderer
lessons.description: This n8n workflow turns a user’s ?query= prompt into a fully rendered, Tailwind-styled HTML page and returns it immediately via the webhook. It first calls OpenAI Chat Completions with a strict JSON Schema (Structured Output) to produce a UI component tree, then a second OpenAI step converts that JSON into {title, html}. Finally, it wraps the result in an HTML template (injecting the Tailwind CDN) and responds with Content-Type: text/html—perfect for rapid prototypes, forms, and simple landing pages.

lessons.title: WooCommerce to Mautic Contact Sync

lessons.title: Gmail Mail Merge with Tracking
lessons.description: This n8n workflow automates same-day customer messaging from a Google Sheet and tracks delivery. It runs on a 1-minute schedule, pulls rows with Status = “Waiting for sending” and today’s Date, emails each contact via Gmail using Title as the subject and Subject as the message, then merges fields. Finally, it updates the matching row (by ID) to Status = “Sent successfully” so you always know what was sent.

lessons.title: Weekday Gmail Outreach Sequencer
lessons.description: This n8n workflow runs every hour on weekdays to send and manage a multi-step outreach sequence sourced from a Google Sheet. If a row hasn’t been contacted (first_emailed is blank) it sends the first HTML email, stamps the sheet with today’s date, and for existing threads it reads Gmail, decodes tracking markers (data-cam, data-seq, data-ph) to determine which follow-up is due based on the “send_on_day” schedule. It then either replies in-thread or starts a new message, safely merges sheet placeholders into the template, and updates the sheet—skipping weekends by design.

lessons.title: HubSpot Customer Onboarding Automation
lessons.description: This n8n workflow automates customer onboarding from a POST webhook: it validates required fields (email, customerName) and starts the sequence. It creates/updates a HubSpot contact, immediately sends a welcome email, then schedules follow-ups—onboarding documents after 2 hours, a personal check-in after 1 day, and a Week-1 Success Guide after 3 days—while updating CRM status and pushing Telegram alerts to the team. It includes a validation-error alert branch and week-1 completion notifications; configure HubSpot (app token) plus Email/Telegram creds and enable the flow to run.

lessons.title: Client Conversation Triage Router
lessons.description: This n8n workflow receives a client conversation via a POST webhook, summarizes it with GPT-4o-mini, and sets department emails (support, admin, sales) to route messages. An LLM “Router Agent” classifies the topic and sends one email to the appropriate department via Gmail, while also posting the summary to Slack and sending a WhatsApp message to the specified recipient. It looks up the client in HubSpot by email and saves the summarized conversation as meeting notes for the contact.

lessons.title: AI-Verified Call-Center Insights Report

It then has a second LLM (DeepSeek Chat) verify the report for accuracy and completeness, returning a JSON verdict with a score and improvement suggestions. Finally, it POSTs the generated report text to a callback URL so you can store or display it downstream.

lessons.title: Automated Parts Quote via Gmail
lessons.description: this n8n workflow checks Gmail for new messages and, if they include spare-parts keywords (TR/DE/EN), triggers an AI quote generator. A Gemini agent pulls customer, BoM, and pricing from three Google Sheets tools, calculates line subtotals and a grand total with the calculator tool, and assembles a complete HTML quote in the sender’s language (without translating part data). It replies to the original email with the HTML quote and marks the thread as read—just add your Gmail/Sheets/Gemini creds and replace the placeholder Sheet IDs.

lessons.title: AI-Controlled Airtable Contact CRUD
lessons.description: This n8n workflow exposes Airtable contact management through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), letting an AI assistant trigger CRUD actions on your base. The MCP Server Trigger accepts AI-provided inputs (Record_ID, Name, email, Assignee, Filter_By_Formula) and routes them to one of four Airtable tools: Get Record, Create Record, Delete Record, or Search Record. Set your Base/Table IDs and webhook path, enable the flow, and the assistant can handle natural-language requests like “add John with john@example.com,” “find contacts assigned to Sarah,” or “delete record XYZ.”

lessons.title: LinkedIn Commenter Leads Extractor
lessons.description: This n8n workflow turns one or more LinkedIn post IDs/URLs (submitted via an in-app form) into a deduped list of commenters by scraping each post with Apify, paginating in 100-comment chunks up to your chosen limit. It then batches the unique commenter profiles (500 per batch) through Apify’s LinkedIn Profile Batch Scraper to enrich them with names, headlines, location, company, and other details, and flattens the results. Finally, it creates a timestamped Google Sheet and appends the enriched leads (or, if you switch modes, exports a CSV instead).

lessons.title: Local Business Contact Extractor
lessons.description: this n8n workflow reads unprocessed queries from a Google Sheet, starts an Apify Google Places scrape, waits until the run finishes, then writes the returned businesses (name, phone, address, website, category) to a Data tab. It filters rows that have websites, loops through each site with Firecrawl to fetch HTML, and a Code node extracts contact details—emails plus LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter—storing them in a Details tab. Finally, it marks each processed website as status = true so subsequent cycles only handle new items.

lessons.title: Apollo Lead Scoring & Outreach
lessons.description: this n8n workflow enriches the lead via Apollo People Match (email, title, organization) and uses a Groq-powered “lead qualifier” to score fit from 1–10 based on industry and job title. It can also be triggered by a webhook or new sheet rows, and is currently inactive until Apollo headers, Gmail OAuth, and the target Sheet are configured.

lessons.title: Research Backed Intro Email Generator

It processes rows where Hasil Riset is empty, uses a Groq-powered analyst with Tavily search to write a company-specific summary and opportunities, saves that back to the sheet/status, then an AI Sales Assistant pulls your email Template and List Product to generate a structured JSON draft (emailSubject, emailBody). Finally, it writes the draft to Send Email Perkenalan and creates a one-click Kirim email link (a webhook URL with the company name URL-encoded) so a human can review and send.

lessons.title: WhatsApp Proposal PDF Generator
lessons.description: This n8n workflow turns incoming WhatsApp messages—voice notes or text—into a tailored business proposal PDF and sends it right back to the user on WhatsApp. It detects message type, downloads/transcribes audio with OpenAI Whisper, then an AI Agent consults Airtable (“Services”) to fuzzy-match the right pack, fills a structured JSON (objectives, inclusions, duration, price, booking link), and renders a branded PDF via APITemplate.io. Finally, it replies on WhatsApp with the proposal attached; optional memory/calculator tools support context and pricing, and the flow is inactive until WhatsApp/OpenAI/Airtable/APITemplate credentials are set.

lessons.title: Telegram Food Delivery Assistant

It also supports quick status/FAQ responses and keeps human-in-the-loop control for payment verification.

lessons.title: LinkedIn Auto-Reply Router
lessons.description: This n8n workflow is a LinkedIn auto-reply router that’s designed to be called by other flows; it accepts a message, sender, chat ID, and optional LinkedIn profile data, then pulls a Notion “Request Router” database to supply example requests and preferred replies as context. A GPT-4o agent with short-term memory (keyed by chat ID) generates a structured response in the shape { "output": "<reply>", "found": <boolean> }, reusing a close match from the database when possible or writing a fresh, on-brand reply when not. The agent is instructed to tailor tone and, when profile metrics are present (followers/connections), adjust behavior (e.g., escalate or politely decline), returning escaped text suitable for Slack or downstream senders.

lessons.title: Chat-to-SQL Database Assistant
lessons.description: This n8n workflow is a chat-based SQL assistant: when a chat message arrives, a GPT-4o-mini agent (with short-term memory) turns natural-language questions into SQL and executes them on Postgres via the built-in Postgres tool. Results are sent back in the same chat, so prompts like “Which tables are available?” work without writing any SQL yourself. The DB node is swappable—use MySQL or SQLite instead of Postgres with the same agent + memory wiring.

On chat messages, a Gemini 2.0 Flash–powered HR assistant with short-term memory queries the vector store via a tool to retrieve relevant passages and answer employee questions grounded in your internal policies. To use it, wire up Google Drive OAuth, Gemini and Pinecone credentials, set the Drive triggers to your folder, and enable the (currently inactive) flow to keep the index fresh and power policy Q&A.

lessons.title: AI Website Booking Chatbot
lessons.description:
This n8n workflow powers a branded website chatbot that collects a visitor’s name, company, email, and project details, checks your Outlook calendar, and books a 30-minute Microsoft Teams meeting.
A GPT-4o agent with short-term memory pulls the next 14 days of events via Microsoft Graph, computes free slots within UK business hours (Mon–Fri, 08:00–17:30 Europe/London), avoids double-booking, and enforces a 48-hour notice window.
If the visitor isn’t ready to book, it sends a formatted enquiry email to your team; otherwise it creates the Outlook event with attendee and description and returns the confirmation via webhook.

lessons.title: Local Qdrant RAG Chatbot
lessons.description:
This n8n workflow builds a compact RAG stack: a form accepts a PDF, loads it, splits the text (chunk 200 / overlap 50), embeds with Ollama’s mxbai-embed-large, and inserts vectors into a Qdrant collection (rag_collection).
A chat trigger connects an Ollama chat model to an agent with short-term memory and a Qdrant “retriever” tool, so it answers questions by pulling the most relevant chunks from your uploaded file.
Set your Qdrant and Ollama creds and enable the flow to chat with your documents end-to-end.

lessons.title: Supabase RAG Chat Assistant
lessons.description: This n8n workflow builds a lightweight RAG chat over a Google Doc: it fetches the doc, splits it into ~1,000-character chunks, embeds each chunk with Together’s BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5, and stores chunk+vector rows in a Supabase table. At query time, a public chat trigger embeds the user message, calls a Supabase RPC (matchembeddings1) to retrieve the top 5 similar chunks, aggregates them, and passes the context to an OpenRouter model (Qwen3-8B) instructed to answer only from those passages. It includes a disabled Telegram trigger for ingestion; once you set Google/Together/Supabase/OpenRouter creds and run the ingest once, the chat is ready to use.

lessons.title: RAG Chat from Uploaded Files
lessons.description: This n8n workflow is a simple, two-part RAG demo: a form lets you upload PDF/CSV files, which are loaded and embedded with OpenAI, then stored in an in-memory vector store keyed vector_store_key. A chat trigger spins up a GPT-4.1 agent that can call a retriever tool backed by the same store, with a cheaper GPT-4.1-mini model driving the vector search. Run the “Load Data” flow to insert vectors, then “Open Chat” to ask questions; note that data clears on restart since the store is in memory.

lessons.title: Legal RAG Q&A Telegram Bot
lessons.description: This n8n workflow is a Telegram-based Legal Assistant that answers user questions by retrieving passages from a Pinecone vector database (“Legal Contract Library”) and generating grounded replies with an OpenAI chat model. It creates embeddings with OpenAI, uses a retrieval-as-tool RAG setup plus a short-term memory window keyed to the Telegram chat ID so follow-ups stay in context, and it’s instructed to say when the source docs don’t contain the answer. After composing the reply it posts back to the same Telegram chat; to use it, connect OpenAI, Pinecone, and Telegram credentials and enable the (currently inactive) flow.

lessons.title: Qdrant RAG Document Updater
lessons.description: This n8n workflow maintains a Qdrant-backed RAG index from Google Drive: it can create a collection, fully clear/rebuild it, and ingest files by splitting (500/50), embedding with OpenAI, and inserting with file_id/file_name metadata. It also supports incremental updates for a single document—delete vectors by file_id, re-download, re-chunk, re-embed, and re-insert—so edits are reflected without a full reindex. A built-in chat (Gemini 1.5 Flash + retriever) queries the chosen Qdrant collection to validate end-to-end answers grounded in your docs.

lessons.title: WhatsApp Knowledge Base Assistant
lessons.description: This n8n workflow is a WhatsApp knowledge-base assistant that accepts text, voice notes, images, and documents, converts them to text (Whisper for audio, vision analysis for images, extractors for PDFs/XLS/XLSX/CSV/HTML/TXT/XML/RTF/ICS), and builds a clean prompt. A GPT-4o-mini agent with short-term memory queries a MongoDB Atlas vector index (OpenAI embeddings, retrieve-as-tool) to pull relevant passages and compose a grounded reply, then sends the answer back to the same WhatsApp chat. A manual path also imports a Google Doc, chunks (3,000/200), embeds, and upserts vectors so the index stays fresh.

lessons.title: Google Docs WhatsApp Support Agent
lessons.description: This n8n workflow powers a WhatsApp AI assistant that answers user messages using your live Google Doc as the knowledge source, with short-term memory per chat. It fetches the doc, builds a prompt with today’s date + doc text + the user’s question, generates a reply with a Gemini-based agent, cleans/normalizes the text, logs it to Google Sheets, and sends the answer back on WhatsApp. If the 24-hour reply window has lapsed it sends a pre-approved template to reopen the conversation (as built, it sends the template only), and you just connect WhatsApp, Google Docs, and LLM creds then enable the flow.

lessons.title: Cal.com Appointment Booking Webhook
lessons.description: This n8n workflow exposes a POST webhook (/appointment-webhook) that either checks availability or books a Cal.com event based on the request payload. When body.tool is checkAvailableSlot, it queries Cal.com /v1/slots using the provided startTime, sets endTime to 18:00 (Asia/Kolkata), includes an eventTypeId, and returns the available windows. Otherwise it creates a 30-minute booking starting at startTime via /v1/bookings using the requester’s name and email, and sends the API response back—configure your Cal.com credentials and real eventTypeId before enabling.

The final text is returned to the webhook for the voice agent; add your InfraNodus API key(s), define the expert names/descriptions, and enable the flow to go live.

lessons.title: Gmail AI Email Classifier
lessons.description:
This n8n workflow polls Gmail every minute, pulls the full contents of each new message, and sends it to a Claude Sonnet-4 agent to classify using a strict policy.
The agent can check prior correspondence via two Gmail tool lookups (from/sent history), read headers like List-Unsubscribe, Precedence, In-Reply-To, and References, then choose a single label—To Respond, FYI, Comment, Notification, Meeting Update, or Marketing—returning only its Label ID.
Finally, the flow applies that label to the message in Gmail via addLabels, so your inbox is auto-organized based on both content and relationship context.

lessons.title: Auto Gmail Labeling Assistant
lessons.description: this n8n workflow pulls recent Gmail messages (read or unread), skips any that already have one of your target labels, and fetches full headers/body for the rest. It feeds the subject and body to an OpenAI (gpt-4.1-nano) agent that returns exactly one category from a fixed set (e.g., Newsletter, Inquiry, Invoice, Proposal, Action Required, etc.). It then checks if that Gmail label exists—creating it if needed—and applies the label to the message so your inbox stays auto-organized.

It’s currently inactive—connect IMAP, Ollama (or your preferred model), and Gmail OAuth to start auto-drafting responses from incoming emails.

lessons.title: AI Inbox Triage and Digest
lessons.description: this workflow watches Gmail, sends the subject/snippet to GPT-4o-mini to return raw JSON (summary, urgency, category, intent), parses it safely, and logs the result (From, Summary, Urgency, Category, Timestamp) to a Google Sheet. If urgency is High or Medium, it posts an “Important Email” alert to Slack and applies a priority Gmail label; otherwise it just adds the general label. At 7:00 PM each day, it builds a Daily Digest of today’s High/Medium items from the sheet and sends it to Slack; the workflow is currently inactive until Gmail, Slack, Sheets, and OpenAI credentials are set.

lessons.description: This n8n “Smart Email Auto-Responder” polls a labeled Gmail inbox hourly, skips internal @syncbricks.com senders and any subject starting with “Re:”, then classifies each new message as Questions, Project Update, or Feedback with a Gemini-powered text classifier. For Questions, it pulls the next three “Available – Office Visit” slots from Google Calendar, emails those options to the sender and adds them as an attendee; for Project Update/Feedback, it sends tailored HTML acknowledgments, then marks the message read and applies a label. Connect Gmail/SMTP and Google Calendar, set your calendar ID and email templates, and enable the (currently inactive) flow to start auto-replying.

lessons.title: AI Customer Support Co-Pilot
lessons.description: This n8n workflow is an AI customer support assistant that ingests requests from Gmail or a chat webhook, extracts structured details (category, urgency, sentiment, product identifiers, etc.), and pulls context from historical support cases in Google Sheets, a product manual in Drive (via PDF extraction), and a mock ERP API. lessons.title: Rolling n8n Workflow Drive Backups
lessons.description: This n8n workflow backs up all your n8n workflows to Google Drive on a 4-hour schedule (or manually), creating a new timestamped folder called “Workflow Backups …”. It calls the n8n API to list workflows, converts each one to a .json file, and uploads the files into that freshly created folder. As housekeeping, it then deletes any older backup folders in the parent directory—so you keep only the latest snapshot (set the Drive parent folder ID and connect your n8n + Google Drive creds).

lessons.title: n8n Error Alerts via Telegram
lessons.description: This n8n “error workflow” listens for failures via On Error, then builds a Telegram-friendly alert that includes the failing workflow’s name and a direct link to the execution. It sends that message to your specified Telegram chat using the Telegram node (add your bot credentials and set the chat ID). To use it, plug in your chat ID/creds and assign this as the Error Workflow for other flows so you get instant Telegram pings on any failure.

Update the target URL, keep your ScrapeNinja/Gemini creds set, enable the flow, and you’ll get JSON data extracted without hand-coding a parser.

lessons.title: Weekly MySQL to Sheets Export
lessons.description:
This n8n workflow runs weekly at 05:00 (server time), queries your MySQL database with SELECT * FROM books;, and takes the returned rows as items.
It then appends those items to a target Google Sheet using OAuth, effectively exporting the books table on a schedule.
Set your MySQL creds, replace the sheetId with your real spreadsheet, and ensure the column order in Sheets matches the query output for clean appends.

lessons.title: Weekly Shodan Unexpected Ports Alert
lessons.description: this n8n workflow fetches a list of watched IPs + expected ports, then queries Shodan for each IP to enumerate open services. It splits those services, compares each port against your allow-list, and—when something unexpected appears—builds a tidy table (HTML→Markdown) with IP, hostnames, port, description, and the raw banner. Finally, it auto-creates a TheHive alert titled “Unexpected ports for <IP>” embedding that table; swap in your IPS endpoint, add the Shodan key and TheHive creds, then enable the (currently inactive) flow.

lessons.description: This n8n workflow analyzes email headers from Gmail or a POST webhook to verify sender authenticity and origin. Finally, it aggregates SPF/DKIM/DMARC results with IP reputation/location into a structured JSON and returns it via the webhook (with a Gmail-trigger path for testing).

lessons.title: Dual-Source SSL Health Monitor
lessons.description:
This n8n workflow runs daily at 10:00, pulls domains from a Notion database, checks each site’s SSL via ssl-checker.io, and (optionally) performs a deep SSL health assessment over SSH using a Node script.
It formats findings—grade, days to expiry, protocol support, vulnerabilities, and recommendations—and posts rich alerts to Discord, including an expiry ping when days_left ≤ 7.
Connect Notion, your SSH private key, and Discord, then enable the (currently inactive) flow to get proactive SSL monitoring and actionable alerts.

lessons.title: Website Scam Risk Evaluator

To use it, add your OpenAI + SerpAPI keys, trigger the form, and read the report in the Evaluator agent’s Logs (the template is inactive by default).

Finally, it posts the formatted blocks to your chosen Slack channel—just set your Jamf Cloud subdomain, OAuth2 creds, software IDs, and Slack channel/creds.

lessons.title: Multi-Agent Tool Use Evaluator
lessons.description: This n8n workflow is a multi-agent evaluation harness: it runs a chat agent with four tools—Qdrant “search_db” (retrieve-as-tool), a one-shot Firecrawl web search, Calculator, and a Summarizer sub-workflow—and captures the agent’s intermediate steps. It can be triggered by live chat or by rows from a Google Sheets dataset; for each row it compares the requested tools_to_call with the tools the agent actually invoked, then writes an evaluation metric tool_called plus the list of actual_tools_called back to the sheet. It uses OpenRouter’s openai/o3 as the LLM, OpenAI embeddings for the Qdrant search_queries collection, and n8n’s Evaluation nodes (checkIfEvaluating, setMetrics) to score tool-use compliance for easy prompt/agent tuning.

lessons.title: LLM Token Usage Cost Tracker
lessons.description:
This n8n template shows how to capture LLM token usage from AI Agents: it runs a sample agent (calls the Think tool twice), then triggers a sub-workflow after execution to process metrics.
That sub-workflow pulls the execution via the n8n API, extracts per-model promptTokens/completionTokens, aggregates them, and appends rows (workflow/execution IDs, name, model, token totals, timestamp) to a Google Sheets “Executions” tab for cost estimating.
Sticky notes walk you through setup (copy the [TEMPLATE] Calculate LLM Token Usage sheet, add n8n + Sheets creds, place the sub-workflow call at the end) and note limits like prompt caching making costs only estimates.

A chat-triggered agent (OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini with short-term memory + MCP client) validates availability and runs the chosen workflow with pass-through parameters, returning the result.

lessons.description:

It supports user-set preferences (vector DB, chat model, embeddings, web tool), uses structured output parsing, and returns the finished template right back to the chat trigger.

lessons.title: Telegram n8n Admin Console
lessons.description: This n8n workflow lets you control your n8n instance from Telegram: list workflows, execute one, activate/deactivate, view recent executions, and show /help, with guardrails for specific chat/user IDs. lessons.title: n8n Workflows GitHub Backup
lessons.description: This n8n workflow backs up your instance’s workflows to GitHub on a daily schedule, filtering to items updated in the last 24 hours. It fetches each workflow, looks up the matching file in the repo, normalizes/compares the JSON (sorted keys), then either creates a new file or edits the existing one with a commit message marking it as “new,” “different,” or skipping when “same.” Config (owner/repo/path) lives in a Set node, optional Slack start/finish notices are included but disabled, and processing runs in batches for lower memory use.

lessons.title: AI GitLab MR Risk Reviewer

It auto-fixes/parses the LLM output, posts a formatted comment back on the MR, builds a project-aware dev/QA distribution list (plus the MR author), and emails a rich HTML report via Gmail. Add your GitLab token, Anthropic API key, and Gmail OAuth, adjust the email mappings, then enable it to get automated review + notification on every MR.

lessons.description:
This n8n workflow takes an image prompt (or your own JPG/PNG/JPEG), generates an image with OpenAI, and hosts it on ImgBB to get a shareable URL.
It then runs that URL through ReSmush.it to shrink the file size and re-uploads the optimized image back to ImgBB, yielding a final, lightweight image URL.
Set your ImgBB API key as query auth (and OpenAI creds if you’re generating images), or skip the generate step and just convert/optimize existing files.

lessons.description:

Configure IMAP, Mindee, and Google Sheets and enable the (currently inactive) flow — and note the subject regex currently misspells “receipt” as reciept.

lessons.title: Invoice Line Items to Airtable
lessons.description:
This n8n workflow has two entry paths: it either watches a Google Drive “Invoices” folder and uploads each new file to LlamaParse (via the LlamaIndex parsing API with a webhook), or it accepts already-parsed invoice JSON through a POST webhook.
When parsed data arrives, it uses OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini) with a strict structured-output schema to normalize line items—description, qty, unit_price, amount—and splits them into individual records.
It then creates an Invoice in Airtable and one linked Line Item per entry, converting prices to numbers and tying each item back to its parent invoice.

lessons.title: Markdown to Notion Page Updater
lessons.description: This n8n workflow takes Markdown-like text (from a mock node or your own source), converts it into Notion-compatible blocks (headings 1–3, paragraphs, quotes, bullets, numbered lists, dividers, and fenced code blocks with language) while preserving basic formatting (bold, italic, links). It also generates a 300-char plain-text excerpt and a block count, then appends the blocks to a Notion page via the Notion API (PATCH /v1/blocks/{page_or_block_id}/children) with batching up to 100 blocks. Run it with the manual trigger, swap the mock text for your real content, and update the Notion endpoint to the page/block you want to fill.

<video_id>.mp4
If uploaded, it sets the file’s sharing to “anyone with the link” and returns a public link.

lessons.title: Supabase Signed URL Uploader
lessons.description:
This Workflow accepts a base64-encoded file (or test form input), maps the MIME type to the appropriate Supabase Storage bucket, and converts it to binary for upload.
It uploads the file to Supabase and generates a time-limited signed URL, returning the full link plus action/status metadata.
It also handles upload and signing failures, emitting structured error responses.

lessons.title: Image-to-PDF via Google Slides
lessons.description:
This Workflow copies a chosen Google Slides template into the target Drive folder and gathers all PNG images there, sorted by creation date.
It then creates one blank slide per image, temporarily makes each image public to insert it, and fits the image to the slide.
Finally, it removes the initial template slide, exports the deck to PDF, and saves the PDF in the same folder with your specified name.

lessons.title: (OCR) Telegram Invoice → SAP
lessons.description:
This Workflow ingests an invoice file sent to a Telegram bot, uploads it to LlamaIndex for OCR, and uses GPT to extract a structured JSON of supplier details, totals, and line items.
It appends the header and each product line to Google Sheets and asks the user in Telegram to confirm sending the data to SAP.
If confirmed, it logs into SAP, builds and posts a PurchaseInvoice from the extracted data, and replies with the created document number.

lessons.title: (OCR) Drive Invoice → Sheets
lessons.description:
This Workflow watches a Google Drive folder for new files, skips any whose IDs are already in a Google Sheet, and downloads each new item.
It uploads the file to Mistral, gets a signed URL, performs OCR (document or image path), stitches page text, then uses Gemini to extract only the fields defined by your sheet headers into strict JSON.
It reinserts the original Drive file ID and appends the structured results to the same Google Sheet for tracking.

lessons.title: (OCR) Invoice → Sheets + Validation
lessons.description:
This Workflow reads a local invoice PDF, extracts the text, and uses an LLM to produce strict JSON of header fields and all line_items (with a fallback parser if needed).
It splits items, generates a per-line Unique Key, and appends them to a Google Sheet.
It then pulls master data, fuzzy-matches each SKU and cost (ASIN + price), and updates the sheet with match status and loss/gain calculations.

lessons.title: Gmail → Invoice Parser to Sheets
lessons.description: This workflow auto-extracts invoice details from labeled Gmail messages and saves them into a structured Google Sheet while organizing the file in Drive. It polls the specified Gmail label every minute, verifies that an attachment exists, converts PDF attachments to text, uses an OpenAI-powered agent to map fields to a fixed JSON schema, creates a timestamped spreadsheet, and moves it into the invoices folder. It then appends the parsed data to the invoice_details sheet with headers, line items, taxes, company and payment info, and will skip emails without attachments or require OCR if the PDF is a scan.

lessons.title: AI Overdue Invoice Follow-Ups
lessons.description: This workflow automates overdue invoice follow-ups by reading a Google Sheet and using recent email history plus AI to decide whether to contact the client and how. It runs on a schedule or manual trigger, computes days since sent, filters for 7, 14, 21, or 28 days, fetches and aggregates recent Gmail conversations with the client, prepares context and templates, then asks OpenAI for a verdict and any necessary template tweaks. If approved, it creates a personalized Gmail draft with an appropriate subject and tone that escalates by interval, and it automatically skips clients contacted about the invoice within the last 72 hours.

lessons.title: Webhook→PDF Invoice Bot
lessons.description: This workflow generates an invoice PDF from incoming order data and distributes it while logging the record. It receives a webhook payload with customer, items, and total, creates a unique invoice ID and checks for duplicates in the Invoices sheet, builds an HTML invoice, converts it to PDF via an external API, uploads the PDF to Google Drive, and emails the customer the invoice with a Pay Now link. It then appends or updates the Google Sheet with status, amount, and Drive link, regenerates the ID if a collision is found, and requires configured API and SMTP credentials for PDF generation and email delivery.

lessons.title: Binance Spot Trader (n8n)
lessons.description: This workflow performs Binance Spot account lookups and order management, including placing market or limit buy/sell orders, fetching open orders, and canceling all open orders. When run manually, it builds query strings for preset trade parameters (symbol BTCUSDT, quantity 0.0001, optional limit price 98000.20, timeInForce GTC), signs them with HMAC SHA256 using the API secret, adds the API key header, and calls the relevant REST endpoints. It returns the raw API responses, and requires a valid Binance API key and secret in “Set Credentials” plus sufficient balances and permissions, with symbols, sizes, and prices editable in the parameter nodes.

lessons.title: Smart HR Screening (n8n)
lessons.description: This workflow screens job applicants from a form and records structured results to a Google Sheet. On submission it uploads the PDF CV to Drive, extracts the text, uses Gemini to pull personal data, education, job history and skills, summarizes the candidate, and combines this with the matching role profile from your JobProfiles sheet. An HR evaluation chain then scores alignment from 1 to 10 with a short justification and the workflow appends city, date, name, email, normalized phone, skills, summary, education, job history, vote, and consideration to the candidates sheet while omitting unknown fields and requiring PDF CVs.

lessons.title: Raw Materials Inventory Automation
lessons.description:
An n8n-powered inventory automation that receives raw-material deliveries via webhook, standardizes the data, logs it to Google Sheets and Supabase, updates Current Stock, and sends low-stock email alerts.
Material issue requests arrive via webhook, generate approval links, validate quantities against available stock, and—when approved—deduct stock and update both Sheets and Supabase.
The system delivers a real-time, auditable flow that reduces manual work, prevents stock drift, and keeps stakeholders notified.

lessons.title: Gemini AI Agent with Memory
lessons.description:
This n8n template creates a public chat AI agent powered by Google Gemini with short-term memory (remembers the last five exchanges).
It equips the agent with LangChain tools—Think for step-by-step reasoning, SerpAPI for live web results, and a Calculator for precise math.
A focused system prompt drives concise, reliable assistance, making it easy to deploy as a personal helper via a chat endpoint.

lessons.title: Linear -> Todoist (One-Way Sync)
lessons.description: This n8n workflow syncs Linear issues to Todoist by listening to create/update/remove events and branching the flow accordingly. It finds an existing Todoist task by Linear issue ID, creates/updates tasks only when the issue has a due date and is assigned to you, enriches sub-issues with a [Parent] → Sub-Issue title, and closes/deletes the Todoist task when the Linear issue is Done or removed. The sync is one-way (Linear → Todoist), targets your chosen Todoist project with a “linear” label, and is easily customized (email filter, states, project/labels).

lessons.title: Host: n8n (EasyPanel)
lessons.description:
📚 What you’ll learn:
In this video, Alexandra shows the simplest way to self-host N8N using EasyPanel and Hetzner — making the process accessible even to beginners. You’ll learn to set up a full server environment with Docker, deploy N8N, and manage everything via a user-friendly interface.
You’ll learn how to:
🔐 Create an SSH key and connect it to Hetzner
🖥️ Spin up a Docker-based server on Hetzner Cloud
⚙️ Install EasyPanel and access it via custom domain
🚀 Deploy N8N in just a few clicks inside EasyPanel
🔄 Update N8N easily via Docker image tags
➕ Install extra apps like Flowise, and monitor resource usage🔥 Why it matters:
Previously, self-hosting N8N required complicated setup and DevOps knowledge. This method provides a visual, beginner-friendly interface while keeping the power and pricing of Hetzner.
🛠️ Tools used:
Hetzner – for cost-effective, high-performance cloud servers
EasyPanel – simple server management and app deployment (Docker-based)
N8N – open-source automation tool
Flowise (optional) – open-source LLM visual builder
Warp terminal – for managing commands
Namecheap – for domain setup (any DNS provider works)

lessons.title: Host: n8n+Flowise (Hz)
lessons.description:
What You Need:
Hostinger account
Domain name (optional, for friendly URLs)Setup Steps:
Get Your Server
Go to Hostinger → Search "Easy Panel"
Select "Add new VPS with Easy Panel"
Choose server size (start with smallest, upgrade later)
Enable daily backups (recommended)
Complete payment
Install n8n
Go to VPS → Manage Panel
Create Easy Panel account
Create new project → Apps → Templates
Search "n8n" → Set version to "latest"
Click Create
Activate License
Open n8n instance
Enter email → Get free license key
Activate (unlocks workflow history, debugging, folders)
Configure Environment Variables
Go to Environment tab
Add: NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL=* (for npm packages)
Add: N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_ENABLED=true (for community nodes)
Save → Deploy
Set Custom Domain (Optional)
Copy VPS IP address
Add A record in your domain DNS
In Easy Panel: Domains → Add domain
Update webhook URL in environment variablesBonus: Install Evolution API (WhatsApp)
Easy Panel → Templates → Search "Evolution API"
Set version to "latest" → Create
Access at: your-url/manager
Get API key from Environment variablesMaintenance:
Update server monthly via terminal
Monitor CPU/memory in dashboard
Upgrade server size if neededCost: $7.99-$11.99/month depending on server size

---
That's it. You now own your automation infrastructure.
